import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Drop rows with missing 'Income' as it's a critical variable for this analysis
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate total spending for each customer across all product categories
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts',
                 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
df['Total_Mnt'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Income and Total Spending,
# with 'Education' level as a categorical differentiator (hue).
# This helps to identify if different education groups have distinct spending patterns
# at various income levels.
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='Income', y='Total_Mnt', hue='Education', palette='viridis', alpha=0.7, s=70)

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Amount Spent vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent on Products', fontsize=12)

# Add a grid for better readability of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust legend position to not overlap with the plot data
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Use tight_layout to ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG image
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
